findings.title: Index allocation contradicts itself and has no allocator
findings.description:
The document gives three different rules for document indices:
- **Output Conventions** says documents draw from 940-949.
- The next paragraph sanctions overflow into "remaining slots in the 900 band."
- **Resolved Design Decisions** repeats "in the 940-949 reserved range. No new convention, no gate change."

Overflowing past 949 is a naming-convention change, so it contradicts both "no change to `file-naming-conventions.md`" and the resolved decision. The 900 band is also not empty space:
- 900 is the Maintenance initiative.
- 901, 906 and 910 are existing maintenance slices.
- 990 is the standing-fixes slice under the project rules.

An index prefix ties a document to a work unit. For example, `303-review.code.*` sits next to slice 303. So a generated `950-analysis.*` or `990-analysis.overview.md` would appear to belong to an unrelated unit. The cause is the per-run increment rule. It fits tech-debt audits, which are independent samples. It does not fit an overview, which is a living document regenerated whenever the plan changes, or a comprehension doc regenerated after every `/understand`. Each rerun burns a slot for good.

The mechanism is also unspecified. The doc never says which component finds "the next free index" (scan `user/analysis/` only, or every `user/` directory?), or what happens once the band is used up.

Fix: give each capability one fixed index, and on rerun either overwrite or supersede it using the `status`/`dateUpdated` fields. Keep per-run increments only for sample-style audits. Remove the overflow paragraph.

findings.title: Tracking `meta.json` makes the staleness warning fire on every run
findings.description:
**Flow step 1** treats a graph as stale when `meta.json`'s `gitCommitHash` differs from `HEAD`. **Working-tree hygiene** requires `knowledge-graph.json` and `meta.json` to stay tracked. These conflict:
1. `/understand` runs at commit X and records X.
2. The user commits the refreshed graph files, which creates X+1.
3. Every later run sees a drift of at least one commit.

A warning that always fires gets ignored. That defeats the stated goal of warning prominently against "a confidently wrong concept doc built on a stale graph."

The check also has unhandled cases:
- `gitCommitHash` missing from history after a rebase, squash or shallow clone, so the commit distance can't be computed.
- Uncommitted working-tree changes, which a hash comparison never sees.

The required "provenance" record has no defined fields (analyzed commit, `lastAnalyzedAt`, plugin version, drift).

Fix: base staleness on whether files outside `.understand-anything/` changed between `gitCommitHash` and `HEAD`. Specify what happens when the hash is unreachable, and define the provenance block.

findings.title: The hard part, getting structure out of the graph, is left unspecified
findings.description:
**Read discipline** says "Grep for the needed section before reading; never load the whole file into context," and asks for a type filter on file-level nodes. Grep cannot reliably pull `layers[]`, `tour[]` and type-filtered `nodes[]` out of JSON:
- It depends on formatting (pretty-printed or minified, key order).
- It violates the project's own parsing rule: parse the meaning, not the layout.
- If it fails, it fails silently, and the concept's Solution Approach ends up empty.

On large repos, even the file-level nodes can number in the thousands, so "file-level only" doesn't bound context size.

The upstream contract is pinned to "v2.8.1" of an "actively developed" plugin, but nothing checks the schema version or required fields. A renamed field upstream would produce empty sections with no error.

Fix: name the extraction method, for example a small Python digest run through Bash, or a tiny `sq` helper that emits a compact summary. Fail loudly when `layers`/`tour`/`nodes` are missing. Cap output size for large graphs.

findings.title: The comprehension analysis doc duplicates the plugin's descriptive output, contradicting "no functional overlap"
findings.description:
**Relationship to the plugin's own skills** says onboard is descriptive, squadron is prescriptive, and there is "no functional overlap." But **Capability 1 Outputs** adds `{index}-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` with "layers, complexity hotspots, entry points, dependency observations." That is a descriptive summary of the same graph that `/understand-onboard` renders.

The prescriptive outputs are the concept and the initiative-plan candidates. The analysis doc is a third artifact per run that burns an index (see the first finding) and goes stale with the graph.

Fix: cut it, or reduce it to a provenance and coverage section inside the concept. Otherwise, rewrite the overlap claim and justify the doc as something more than an onboard restatement.

findings.title: Capability 1 does not say what happens to existing documents or a missing `project-documents/` tree
findings.description:
**Outputs** fixes `project-documents/user/project-guides/000-concept.{project}.md` and puts interview answers in the protected **User-Provided Concept** section. Several things are undefined:
- **Rerun or existing concept.** The section can never be rewritten, so a second run cannot update it, and the doc doesn't say whether the skill refuses, writes a sibling, or appends.
- **Target repo with no squadron layout.** The motivating case, a codebase "never planned in squadron," has no `project-documents/user/` and no guide install. The doc doesn't say whether the skill scaffolds the layout, calls `cf`, or stops.
- **Source of `{project}`.** The graph's `project` field, `cf` config, or the PM?
- **Initiative-plan candidates.** Where they are shown (chat, or a section of the analysis doc?) and where an accepted candidate is written. In squadron's own repo, `001-initiative-plan.squadron.md` already exists, so the choice between merge and overwrite is load-bearing.
- **Status value.** Which enum `status` the generated documents carry.

findings.title: Capability 2's status source is ambiguous in the real input
findings.description:
The **Document field schema** derives Status from "Initiative statuses," and **Translation rules** require "Status is honest." The primary input has two status signals that can disagree.

In `001-initiative-plan.squadron.md`, entry 13 (900) is `[x]`, which reads as done, yet its text says `Status: not_started`. The document names neither as authoritative, so the overview could report it either way.

Initiative-level status is also coarse. An in-progress initiative with most slices merged looks the same as one with none. The doc doesn't say whether slice plans or task files are consulted.

Separately, the "Risks / Open Questions" field comes from "Initiative plan notes," a section the initiative plan does not have.

findings.title: "Derive, never invent" conflicts with the interview and with the features-to-outcomes rewrite
findings.description:
Three statements pull against the derive-only rule:
- **Design Goals** say the client document "restates existing approved artifacts… not a place where new claims… appear."
- **Capability 2 Inputs** say that without a concept, the skill "sources purpose from the initiative plan plus interview." Interview answers are not an approved artifact, so they are new claims.
- **Translation rules** require "Features become outcomes." Turning a feature into an outcome is itself a new claim. The doc's own example asserts "converges without human babysitting," which no input states.

The doc never says how a claim's trace back to its source is recorded or checked.

Fix: either keep a source map beside the generated overview, or state that interview answers are written into a concept first, so the overview only ever reads artifacts.

findings.title: Emphasis parameter is both specified and rejected
findings.description:
**Translation rules** say "Emphasis is a generation parameter." **Resolved Design Decisions** say there is one neutral document, and that an emphasis parameter "is added only if real use demonstrates the need." A slice designer cannot tell whether `/sq:overview` takes an argument.

Fix: delete the Translation-rules sentence.

findings.title: The overview is put in the analysis category the doc rejects for it elsewhere
findings.description:
**Delivery** keeps `overview` out of the `sq:analysis` dispatcher because "nothing about it audits a codebase… would make that dispatcher's name inaccurate." **Output Conventions** then puts the same artifact in `user/analysis/`, with `docType: analysis`, in the range the naming convention reserves for "codebase analysis, research, investigation."

The principle "separation of audience is a document boundary" is then expressed only as a filename word. `cf` introspection and the downstream phases will treat a stakeholder overview as engineering analysis.

Avoiding a gate change is a fair reason. But the doc should name this trade-off openly instead of calling the placement natural.

findings.title: Gitignore scope leaves `intermediate/` tracked by default
findings.description:
The contract table lists `intermediate/scan-result.json` as kept upstream for incremental runs, and says squadron does not touch it. The only ignore entry is `.understand-anything/.trash-*/`, and the "Not ignored" list omits `intermediate/`. So machine-specific incremental state gets committed by default.

This policy also lands in client repos. Committing a large, frequently regenerated `knowledge-graph.json` causes diff churn and merge conflicts, and the doc doesn't weigh that.

The "idempotent" check is also undefined. If a repo already ignores `.understand-anything/` entirely, the skill's assumption that the graph is tracked breaks without anyone noticing.

findings.title: Checking that the plugin is installed is unnecessary and fragile
findings.description:
Flow step 1 says "verify the plugin is installed." The only way to do that is to inspect Claude Code's undocumented plugin storage. The real precondition is that `knowledge-graph.json` exists and is valid, and **Architectural Principles** already frame the graph as "an input, not a dependency."

Drop the plugin check and keep only the graph check.

findings.title: Dependency [100] has the wrong rationale
findings.description: **Dependencies** cite [100] for "CLI command registration," but neither capability adds a CLI command. (a) is explicitly "no installer, manifest, or CLI change," and (b) is a markdown file in `commands/sq/`. The real dependency is the `install-commands` copy mechanism.

findings.title: Translation-rule examples are hallucination traps in the skill prompts
findings.description:
The squadron-specific examples ("Initiative 140 status draft" → "foundational work, in progress"; "Weighted review convergence…" → "automated review that converges…") are likely to be copied into the `/sq:overview` prompt. Placed next to "derive, never invent," they are exactly the trap CLAUDE.md warns about: phrasing a model will reuse for unrelated projects.

The first example also uses `draft`, which **Output Conventions** says the gate rejects.

Fix: keep the examples out of the shipped prompt, or make them abstract.
